questions.stem: A team wants to query Lambda logs by fields such as requestId, userId and orderStatus in CloudWatch Logs Insights. How should the functions write their logs?

options.text: As free-form text sentences that mention each field's value
options.rationale: Free text needs fragile parsing in every query.

options.text: As print statements with no named fields
options.rationale: Unstructured output cannot be filtered by field.

options.text: As structured JSON, with those fields as keys
options.rationale: Logs Insights discovers JSON fields so queries can filter and group on them.

options.text: To a local file in /tmp
options.rationale: Files in /tmp are lost when the environment is recycled and are not in CloudWatch Logs.

questions.explanation: Structured logging makes logs searchable and easy to turn into metrics.

questions.stem: A Lambda function must publish a custom business metric on every invocation, without adding a synchronous CloudWatch API call to each request. What should the developer use?

options.text: A PutMetricData API call from the handler on every invocation
options.rationale: This adds a synchronous API call to each request.

options.text: X-Ray annotations on each trace
options.rationale: Annotations index traces; they are not CloudWatch metrics.

options.text: An Amazon SNS message for each value
options.rationale: SNS delivers messages; it does not create metrics.

options.text: Embedded metric format (EMF) in the function's log output
options.rationale: CloudWatch extracts the metric from the structured log event asynchronously.

questions.explanation: EMF lets code emit metrics through logs, with no extra API call.

questions.stem: An application on Amazon EC2 instances must publish a custom metric for the number of items in an in-memory queue. Which approaches will publish it to CloudWatch? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Enable detailed monitoring on the EC2 instances that run the app
options.rationale: Detailed monitoring adds one-minute EC2 metrics, not application values.

options.text: Send the value to the CloudWatch agent through StatsD
options.rationale: The agent collects custom metrics, for example through StatsD, and publishes them to CloudWatch.

options.text: Change the X-Ray sampling rate
options.rationale: Sampling controls tracing, not metrics.

options.text: Call PutMetricData from the application through the AWS SDK
options.rationale: PutMetricData publishes custom metric data points.

options.text: Turn on AWS CloudTrail data events
options.rationale: CloudTrail records API activity, not application values.

questions.explanation: Custom metrics come from PutMetricData, the CloudWatch agent or embedded metric format logs.

questions.stem: A team wants an email when a Lambda function's error count goes above 10 in five minutes. Which combination of steps will meet this requirement? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Create an X-Ray group with a filter expression for requests that have errors
options.rationale: Groups organize traces; they do not send email.

options.text: Create a CloudWatch alarm on the Errors metric that notifies the topic
options.rationale: The alarm changes state when the threshold is crossed and sends a notification to the SNS topic.

options.text: Set a CloudWatch Logs retention policy on the function's log group
options.rationale: Retention controls how long logs are kept.

options.text: Create an Amazon SNS topic and confirm an email subscription to it
options.rationale: SNS delivers each notification to the confirmed email subscribers of the topic.

options.text: Add an X-Ray sampling rule that traces every failed request
options.rationale: Sampling rules decide which requests are traced; they do not send notifications.

questions.explanation: Alarms watch a metric and act when they change state, and an SNS topic with an email subscription turns that into an email. X-Ray groups and sampling rules are the nearest distractors, but they organize traces and send nothing.

questions.stem: Developers want an email each time an AWS CodePipeline execution succeeds or fails. What should the developer configure?

options.text: A CloudWatch Logs metric filter on the CodeBuild logs that counts failed builds
options.rationale: Build logs do not carry the pipeline's overall result in a reliable way.

options.text: An EventBridge rule for pipeline state changes that targets an SNS topic
options.rationale: CodePipeline emits state-change events that rules can route to notifications.

options.text: A manual approval action at the end of the pipeline
options.rationale: Approvals pause the pipeline; they do not notify on completion.

options.text: AWS CloudTrail Insights
options.rationale: CloudTrail Insights detects unusual API activity.

questions.explanation: Deployment and pipeline events flow through EventBridge, which can notify on completion.

questions.stem: A team wants to be warned before its Lambda functions reach the account's concurrency limit. What should a CloudWatch alarm watch?

options.text: The average Duration metric of the busiest function, measured over five minutes
options.rationale: Duration measures run time, not concurrency.

options.text: The Invocations metric of one function
options.rationale: Invocations count requests, not concurrent instances.

options.text: ClaimedAccountConcurrency compared with the account's concurrency quota
options.rationale: Lambda uses this metric to track how much account concurrency is already claimed, including reserved and provisioned concurrency.

options.text: The number of Lambda Invoke events recorded by CloudTrail
options.rationale: CloudTrail events are API records, not a concurrency measure.

questions.explanation: Lambda's documentation recommends alarming on ClaimedAccountConcurrency against the quota; ConcurrentExecutions alone can understate what is claimed.

questions.stem: A developer wants to search X-Ray traces by customer ID to investigate one customer's slow requests. How should the code record the customer ID?

options.text: As metadata on the segment
options.rationale: Metadata is stored with the trace but is not indexed for search.

options.text: As a CloudWatch metric dimension
options.rationale: Metric dimensions do not make traces searchable.

options.text: In the function's environment variables
options.rationale: Environment variables are configuration, not per-request data.

options.text: As an annotation on the segment
options.rationale: Annotations are indexed, so filter expressions can search on them.

questions.explanation: Use annotations for values you filter on and metadata for extra detail.

questions.stem: A developer wants end-to-end traces for requests that go through an API Gateway REST API, a Lambda function and DynamoDB. Which steps are needed? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Turn on CloudTrail data events for the DynamoDB table and the function
options.rationale: CloudTrail records API calls for auditing, not traces.

options.text: Enable detailed CloudWatch metrics on the API Gateway stage
options.rationale: Detailed metrics do not connect a request's path across services.

options.text: Turn on active tracing for the function and instrument its SDK calls
options.rationale: Lambda records its segment, and instrumentation records the DynamoDB calls.

options.text: Enable VPC Flow Logs
options.rationale: Flow logs record network traffic metadata, not request traces.

options.text: Enable X-Ray tracing on the API Gateway stage
options.rationale: API Gateway then starts or continues the trace for each request.

questions.explanation: Tracing must be on at each hop, plus SDK instrumentation for downstream calls.

questions.stem: An Application Load Balancer keeps routing requests to instances whose application has stopped responding. The health check uses the default path /, which the web server still answers. What should the developer change?

options.text: Point the target group's health check at an application path such as /health
options.rationale: The load balancer stops routing to targets that fail the check.

options.text: Increase the load balancer's idle timeout so that slow targets have more time to answer
options.rationale: Idle timeout affects connection reuse, not health.

options.text: Turn on access logs
options.rationale: Access logs record requests; they do not take targets out of service.

options.text: Add a second listener on port 443
options.rationale: Another listener does not detect unhealthy targets.

questions.explanation: Health checks should exercise the application, not just the port.

questions.stem: On Amazon EKS, new pods receive traffic before they finish loading their cache, and early requests fail. What should the developer add to the pod specification?

options.text: A liveness probe that restarts the pod when the cache is missing
options.rationale: Liveness probes restart containers; restarts would not stop early traffic.

options.text: A readiness probe that succeeds once the cache is loaded
options.rationale: Pods receive traffic only once their readiness probe succeeds.

options.text: A larger memory limit
options.rationale: More memory does not delay traffic until the pod is ready.

options.text: An extra replica of the deployment
options.rationale: More pods still receive traffic too early.

questions.explanation: Readiness controls traffic; liveness controls restarts.

questions.stem: A team wants its Lambda functions' logs in JSON, and wants only WARN and higher messages from the application code to reach CloudWatch Logs. The team does not want to change the function code. Which combination of settings will meet these requirements? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Set each function's log format to JSON
options.rationale: Lambda's advanced logging controls can emit logs in JSON without code changes.

options.text: Turn on active tracing with AWS X-Ray
options.rationale: Tracing records requests, not log format or log level.

options.text: Use the embedded metric format for every log line
options.rationale: EMF creates metrics from logs; it does not filter by log level.

options.text: Set each function's application log level to WARN
options.rationale: Lambda then filters out application logs below WARN before sending them to CloudWatch Logs.

options.text: Set the log group's retention period to one day
options.rationale: Retention deletes old logs; it does not filter by level.

questions.explanation: Lambda advanced logging controls set log format and log-level filtering per function.

questions.stem: An order passes through an API, an Amazon SQS queue and three Lambda functions. When something goes wrong, developers struggle to find all the log lines for one order across the services. What should the developer do?

options.text: Write every service's logs to one shared log group
options.rationale: Mixing logs in one group does not link the lines for a given order.

options.text: Raise the log level to DEBUG in every one of the services so that more detail is logged
options.rationale: More log lines make the search harder, not easier.

options.text: Log a correlation ID in every entry and pass it with each message
options.rationale: One ID shared across services lets a single query find every log line for the order.

options.text: Keep the logs for a longer retention period
options.rationale: Retention keeps logs longer; it does not connect them.

questions.explanation: Propagate a correlation (or trace) ID through every hop and include it in structured logs.

questions.stem: An application on EC2 instances writes lines containing "PAYMENT_FAILED" to a CloudWatch Logs log group. The team wants an alarm when more than five such lines appear in five minutes. The application code must not change. What should the developer create first?

options.text: A subscription filter that streams the logs to Amazon Data Firehose
options.rationale: Streaming the logs elsewhere does not create a metric to alarm on.

options.text: An X-Ray annotation named PAYMENT_FAILED on each failed request
options.rationale: That requires code changes and is for traces, not log-based alarms.

options.text: A Logs Insights query that runs every five minutes from a script
options.rationale: This needs custom scheduling code when a metric filter does the job.

options.text: A metric filter on the log group that counts PAYMENT_FAILED lines
options.rationale: The metric filter turns matching log lines into a metric, and the alarm watches that metric.

questions.explanation: CloudWatch Logs metric filters create metrics from log patterns without code changes.

questions.stem: A container on Amazon EKS sometimes deadlocks: the process keeps running but stops answering requests, and it stays that way until someone restarts it. How can the developer have Kubernetes restart it automatically?

options.text: Add a liveness probe on a health endpoint
options.rationale: When the liveness probe keeps failing, Kubernetes restarts the container.

options.text: Add a readiness probe that calls the same endpoint
options.rationale: A failing readiness probe removes the pod from service but does not restart it.

options.text: Raise the container's memory limit in the pod spec
options.rationale: A deadlock is not a memory problem.

options.text: Increase the number of replicas in the Deployment
options.rationale: More replicas spread the load, but the stuck container stays stuck.

questions.explanation: Liveness probes restart unhealthy containers; readiness probes control whether a pod receives traffic.

questions.stem: An application handles millions of requests a day with AWS X-Ray tracing turned on. Tracing every request costs too much, but the team still wants a representative picture of performance. What should the developer configure?

options.text: Turn off tracing and rely on CloudWatch Logs alone
options.rationale: This loses the request-level view that traces give.

options.text: X-Ray sampling rules that trace a share of requests
options.rationale: Sampling rules control how many requests are recorded, keeping costs down while traces stay representative.

options.text: Record every request with annotations removed to save space
options.rationale: Annotations are small; the cost comes from the number of traces.

options.text: Put all traces into a single X-Ray group to reduce stored data
options.rationale: Groups filter traces for viewing; they do not change how many requests are recorded.

questions.explanation: X-Ray sampling rules set how many requests are traced, by fixed rate and reservoir.

questions.stem: A developer wants to attach a large JSON object with debugging details to X-Ray segments. The data does not need to be searchable in trace filters. How should the code record it?

options.text: As an annotation on the segment
options.rationale: Annotations are indexed key-value pairs for filtering, meant for simple values.

options.text: As the segment's name
options.rationale: The segment name identifies the service, not debugging data.

options.text: As metadata on the segment
options.rationale: Metadata holds any data you want stored with the trace; it is not indexed for searching.

options.text: As a CloudWatch metric dimension
options.rationale: Dimensions are for metrics and do not attach data to traces.

questions.explanation: Use annotations for indexed values to filter on, and metadata for other data you want kept with the trace.

questions.stem: A team wants to be notified when its usage of an AWS service gets close to an account quota, before requests start failing. What should the developer configure?

options.text: An AWS CloudTrail trail that logs every call to the service
options.rationale: CloudTrail records API calls; it does not compare usage with quotas.

options.text: An EventBridge rule that matches every service API call
options.rationale: This produces a flood of events and no quota comparison.

options.text: A Lambda function that requests a quota increase every day
options.rationale: Automatic increase requests are not monitoring and may be denied.

options.text: A CloudWatch alarm on usage compared with the quota
options.rationale: Usage metrics can be compared with the applied quota, so the alarm fires before the limit is reached.

questions.explanation: Service Quotas and CloudWatch usage metrics support alarms that warn before a quota is reached.

questions.stem: A team wants to check its public API's checkout flow from outside AWS every five minutes, as a user would, and be alerted if the flow breaks even when no real users are active. What should the developer set up?

options.text: A CloudWatch Synthetics canary that runs the flow on a schedule
options.rationale: Canaries are scripts that run on a schedule against endpoints and report failures.

options.text: An Application Load Balancer health check on the checkout path
options.rationale: ALB health checks test targets from inside the VPC, not the full user flow.

options.text: A CloudWatch alarm on the API's 5XXError metric
options.rationale: With no real traffic, there are no errors to alarm on.

options.text: X-Ray tracing on the API and its backend services
options.rationale: Tracing records real requests; it does not create test traffic.

questions.explanation: Synthetic monitoring finds breakages before users do, even with no traffic.

questions.stem: A service has separate CloudWatch alarms for high latency and for a high error rate. On-call developers receive too many notifications when only one of them briefly fires. They want to be paged only when both are in ALARM at the same time. What should the developer create?

options.text: A metric math expression that adds latency and the error rate together
options.rationale: A sum of unrelated metrics has no meaningful threshold.

options.text: A composite alarm that combines the two alarms with AND
options.rationale: Composite alarms evaluate a rule over other alarms, so they notify only when both are in ALARM.

options.text: A shorter evaluation period on both of the existing alarms
options.rationale: Shorter periods make the alarms fire more often, not less.

options.text: A second SNS topic for each of the existing alarms
options.rationale: More topics do not combine the alarm conditions.

questions.explanation: Composite alarms reduce alarm noise by combining the states of other alarms.
